title: Safe Subnet Decommissioner and Delegated DNS Failover
author: Ethan Morales
description:
Motivation: customers running long-lived private control planes need a predictable, auditable way to retire subnets during AZ maintenance, capacity rebalancing, or decommission workflows without causing DNS holes or transient routing blackholes. This PR introduces a coordinated 'Safe Subnet Decommissioner' workflow plus a delegated DNS failover mechanism (DNS Bridge) to ensure control-plane endpoints remain resolvable during and after subnet lifecycle changes.

What changed (high level): added a new terraform module (subnet-decommissioner) that emits lifecycle hooks and necessary IAM roles; extended the installer Helm chart with a decommission-controller deployment that watches SubnetLifecycle annotations and orchestrates: route table reassociation, ENI graceful detach, ephemeral private IP reallocation, security-group staged rotate, and a DNS Bridge that creates temporary delegated records in a customer-managed hosted zone to maintain reachability. Also added a small operator (go microservice) used by the Helm chart to drive the steps and emit audit events.

Design notes: the decommissioner minimizes blast radius by performing operations in phases with feature-flagged concurrency limits per-AZ, emitting progress events to the control plane audit log, and validating that at least one healthy control-plane endpoint remains reachable before final subnet deletion. The DNS Bridge uses conditional Route53 delegation into a short-lived subdomain (e.g. decomm-<cluster>.redwood-internal) and an SRV to A rewrite to route traffic to standby endpoints in surviving subnets. We intentionally avoid changing customer primary hosted zones; delegation keys are ephemeral and rotated by the controller.

Migration & rollout: phased rollout behind a feature flag (installer config flag: enableSubnetDecommissioner). Default off for existing customers. When enabled, operator runs in 'dry-run' mode for 48 hours and reports suggested actions via the console. After a continuous integration smoke window and manual sign-off, the flag can be flipped to live. A reversible 'recompose' step allows re-adding previously decommissioned subnets.

Testing: unit tests for the operator (mock AWS APIs), integration tests in the benchlab that simulate AZ failover, and an e2e scenario in the perf-canary that runs a 24h decommission+recovery cycle. CI includes terraform plan validation, helm lint, go unit tests, and a staged infra apply in the ephemeral test account.

Rollback plan: controller supports a 'cancel-decommission' annotation which reverses route table changes and reattaches ENIs where possible; DNS Bridge entries are removed only after controller verifies client-side reachability via probe hooks. If a roll-forward is required, operator can accelerate by applying a 'force-commit' annotation but that requires an explicit engineer confirmation step logged to audit.

Related work: ties to ENG-12540 (subnet lifecycle orchestration), ENG-13008 (dns-resilience), and the private-installer upgrade playbook.

Notes: this PR is intentionally conservative about IAM scope (least-privilege roles for the operator) and includes thorough audit logging for compliance customers.

Ethan Morales: Yes — updated the role template to exclude TerminateInstances and added a new step that uses a delegated escalation token for infra-team signed termination (audit only).
Lars Engel: The DNS Bridge sounds useful but we should avoid touching customer apex zones. Confirmed we only create delegated subdomains and ephemeral NS records — LGTM.
Maya Chen: Add an integration test that simulates NAT gateway failover; otherwise looks good.
Ethan Morales: Added NAT failover test to benchlab and validated end-to-end routing during decommission.

release_notes: Introduces a Safe Subnet Decommissioner operator and DNS Bridge to enable controlled subnet retirement and DNS failover for private control planes. Feature disabled by default; opt-in via installer flag. Includes terraform module, Helm chart, operator, tests, and runbook.
